title: Conclusion holds both major low-code platforms in separate opcos, so sell to the opco
content:
Conclusion is a federation of roughly 40 operating companies, and the screen records that it holds both major low-code platforms — Mendix through Conclusion Low Code Company and OutSystems through myAppX and myBrand — alongside SAP, Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics and AFAS. The conclusion drawn is procedural: sell to the opco, not the group.

The reason is that a federation has no single stack to complement or displace. Each opco carries its own platform relationship, its own vertical and its own delivery economics, so an assessment made at group level is an average of positions that contradict each other. A pitch aimed at the holding company also aims at a buyer who does not run delivery and therefore cannot adopt anything.

This puts Conclusion in the same handling class as the other federated groups in the workbook rather than in the same class as the disqualified single-stack firms. The row is filed do-not-pitch at group level, which is a statement about the entry point, not a judgement that all 40 subsidiaries are unqualified. Any real work here starts by naming the opco and re-running the screen on it alone.
